title: Locker Rental: abandoned property hold and disposal-eligibility timing after closure
content:
## Scope
This document covers the Locker Rental product line. It states how long property left behind in a locker is held after the rental closes, and when that property becomes eligible for disposal. The specific hold period and disposal-eligible period that this rule reads for a given tier are fixed in the Locker Rental inspection frequency and abandoned property terms; this document states only the timing rule itself.

## Rule
Once a rental closes, any property left in the locker is held for the tier's fixed hold period, and may be disposed of once the tier's fixed disposal-eligible period has elapsed since the closure. Both periods are counted as whole calendar days, with no rounding down of a partial day into a full day.

## Equivalent restatement
- Anchor: the moment the rental closed.
- Hold period: the tier's fixed number of full calendar days during which left-behind property is held from that anchor.
- Disposal eligibility: reached once the tier's fixed disposal-eligible number of full calendar days has elapsed from that same anchor.

## Boundary case (hypothetical)
Suppose, purely as an illustration, a tier's hold period were fixed at 20 calendar days and its disposal-eligible period at 40 calendar days, and a rental closed at the start of a given day. Property would be held through the 20th full calendar day after closure. Disposal would not become eligible until the 40th full calendar day after closure had fully elapsed; an attempt on the 39th day would be one day short of that period, while the 40th day itself would satisfy it.

## Points of judgement
The hold period and the disposal-eligible period are two separate figures counted from the same closure anchor, not one figure applied twice; a tier's disposal-eligible period runs longer than its hold period in every case the source fixes, so property remains held, but not yet eligible for disposal, for the span between the two.
